topic: EU AI Act obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models: requirements, systemic-risk models, code of practice and deadlines

key_points.point: GPAI provider obligations began applying on 2 August 2025: technical documentation, information for downstream providers, an EU copyright policy, and a public summary of training content.
A model trained with more than 10^25 FLOP is presumed to have high-impact capabilities and thus systemic risk; the Commission can also designate models and amend thresholds by delegated act.

Systemic-risk providers must additionally evaluate models (including adversarial testing), assess and mitigate systemic risks, report serious incidents to the AI Office, and ensure cybersecurity (Article 55).
Providers must notify the Commission without delay and within two weeks of meeting or foreseeing the 10^25 FLOP threshold, and may argue the model is not systemic-risk.
Commission guidelines treat a model trained with more than about 10^23 FLOP that can generate language, text-to-image or text-to-video as indicatively general-purpose.

Free and open-source models are exempt from some documentation and EU-representative duties, but not from copyright policy and training-summary duties, and the exemption never applies to systemic-risk models.
The GPAI Code of Practice, published 10 July 2025, has Transparency, Copyright and Safety and Security chapters; the last applies only to systemic-risk providers.
The Commission and AI Board deemed the Code an adequate voluntary tool; signing brings reduced burden and more legal certainty, while non-signers must show compliance by other adequate means.
Most major providers signed the Code (including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and Amazon); xAI signed only the Safety and Security chapter.
The Commission's enforcement powers over GPAI providers, including fines of up to 3% of worldwide annual turnover or EUR 15 million (whichever is higher), have applied since 2 August 2026.
Models placed on the EU market before 2 August 2025 have until 2 August 2027 to comply.
The Digital Omnibus on AI (in force 27 July 2026) postponed high-risk obligations (Annex III to 2 December 2027, Annex I to 2 August 2028) but did not postpone GPAI obligations.
On 14 October 2026 the AI Office sent its first formal requests for information to providers of GPAI models with systemic risk: the first use of its investigative powers.
